== con-leche/ConLeche/MainTheorem.lean#L90-L117
    90  /-- **The main theorem.**  Every environment the checker accepts has a
    91  model in every set theory — at every `Nat.div`/`Nat.mod` pin list, so
    92  consistency does not depend on which variants the install gate is
    93  handed (the empty list included: under it every stream that declares
    94  `Nat.div` declines).  The shipped binary runs the fold at
    95  `natOpPinSets`. -/
    96  theorem model_exists (V : Type w) [SetTheory V]
    97      (pins : List NatOpPinSet) (ds : Array Declaration) (env : Env)
    98      (accepted : checkDecls .verified pins ds = .ok env) :
    99      Nonempty (Model V env) := by
   100    obtain ⟨m⟩ := Cached.checkDecls_sound (V := V) rfl accepted
   101    exact ⟨Model.Model.ofEnvModelM m⟩
   102  
   103  open Frontend in
   104  /-- **The main corollary.**  A file declaring a theorem of type `False`
   105  in the shape `jsonWithTheoremFalse` describes is rejected: the parse
   106  reads the template's four lines into a theorem record of type `False`,
   107  the preparation keeps the record, and a stream holding it is never
   108  accepted.  At every pin list, as the main theorem: the shipped binary
   109  runs the fold at `natOpPinSets`. -/
   110  theorem no_False_declaration (V : Type w) [SetTheory V]
   111      (pins : List NatOpPinSet) (chunks : List ByteArray)
   112      (h : jsonWithTheoremFalse chunks) :
   113      ∃ e, (do
   114        let pre ← builtinPreludeE
   115        let r ← parseChunks chunks
   116        let ds := preparePrelude pre r.decls
   117        checkDecls .verified pins ds) = .error e := by

== con-leche/ConLeche/Verify/Cached/MainC.lean#L49-L55
    49  /-- **Acceptance**: what the fold accepts carries the model. -/
    50  theorem checkDecls_sound (hμ : μ.verifiedChecks = true)
    51      {ds : Array Declaration} {env' : Env}
    52      (h : checkDecls μ pins ds = .ok env') :
    53      Nonempty (EnvModelM V μ env') := by
    54    obtain ⟨fc, rfl⟩ := checkDecls_fullyChecked μ h
    55    exact fullyChecked_sound V hμ fc

== crates/con-ron/src/bin/con-ron.rs#L87-L212
    87  usage: con-ron [--verified|--trusted] [--jobs=<n>] [--no-mark-persistent]
    88                 [--progress[=<stride>]] [--pins FILE|--no-pins]
    89                 FILE.ndjson
    90         con-ron --help
    91  
    92    (C), the Rust arena checker of con-ron's DESIGN.md section 8: con-leche's
    93    pure checker over an append-only DAG of per-constructor handle arrays, with
    94    con-leche's command line and con-leche's exit codes, so that
    95    scripts/diff-e2e.sh can run the same 383 fixtures against this binary and
    96    the Lean twin `con-ron-lean` alike.  A term is a u32 handle into a Vec: on
    97    the checking path there is no Arc, no tagged pointer and no reference count
    98    at all.  (The PINNED DATA the checker compares against is still
    99    con-leche's own constants as Expr values, interned into the persistent tier
   100    once at startup -- crates/con-ron-core/src/lib.rs says why.)
   101  
   102    --verified        the default, and the mode the main theorem is about: every
   103                      environment the fold accepts in this mode has a model in
   104                      every set theory (ConLeche.model_exists), so a stream
   105                      declaring a theorem of type False is never accepted.  The
   106                      same two statements are PROVED about this program's
   107                      pipeline (ConRon.Capstone.model_exists and
   108                      no_False_declaration, on the Aeneas model of the Rust),
   109                      using only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and
   110                      Quot.sound.  What they still assume are hypotheses, not
   111                      axioms: that the driver runs the extracted stages in the
   112                      order it does on the file's bytes, and that the
   113                      unextracted Rust in-process modeller answers as the Lean
   114                      twin's does.  They hold at every pin text, every prelude
   115                      and both settings of the CON_LECHE_INMODEL* switches.
   116                      OVERVIEW.md section 3.1 lists them.
   117    --trusted         the unverified mode: the SAME checker bodies at the mode
   118                      with the certification-only work switched off.  An accept
   119                      in this mode is outside the theorem.
   120    --jobs=<n>        the check phase runs on <n> worker threads sharing the
   121                      persistent tier and the installed index by reference
   122                      (DESIGN.md section 8.3): each worker owns a scratch tier,
   123                      its own caches and a copy of the pin handles, and the
   124                      results are merged by record index and walked in record
   125                      order, so the verdict and the record a rejection names are
   126                      the same at every <n>.  Default: one per hardware thread,
   127                      capped at 16.  A worker reserves 1 GiB of stack, which a
   128                      `ulimit -v` must allow for.  0 or a non-numeral is a usage
   129                      error, as in con-leche.
   130    --no-mark-persistent
   131                      ACCEPTED AND A NO-OP, for a stronger reason than the
   132                      `con-ron` binary's: the mark it turns off is a
   133                      Lean-runtime reference-counting device
   134                      (Runtime.markPersistent), and this checker has no
   135                      reference counts at all -- a term is a u32 handle into a
   136                      Vec and the persistent tier is immutable in phase B.  A
   137                      run that passes it says so on stderr.
   138    --progress[=<stride>]
   139                      opt-in progress heartbeat on STDERR, one line shape per
   140                      phase:
   141                        con-ron: parse done: <N> fold records ... t=<s>s
   142                        con-ron: install <i>/<N> <decl> t=<s>s
   143                        con-ron: install done: <N>/<N> ..., <M> pending
   144                        con-ron: check <done>/<M> <kind> <name> t=<s>s
   145                        con-ron: check done: <M>/<M> t=<s>s
   146                        con-ron: done: parse <p>s, install <i>s, check <c>s
   147                      An install line is printed BEFORE every <stride>-th
   148                      declaration is installed, so a run that dies in the
   149                      install phase names the declaration it died in on its last
   150                      line; a check line is printed AFTER every <stride>-th
   151                      COMPLETED check.  On a failure the phase's closing line
   152                      says so and the summary still prints.  Bare --progress is
   153                      stride 1; a stride that is not a decimal numeral, or 0, is
   154                      a usage error.
   155    --pins FILE       con-ron's own, FOR TESTING: read the pin list from a
   156                      `con-ron-pins/1` dump instead of the core's own embedded
   157                      text (task #43), through the UNVERIFIED reader.  The pins
   158                      are interned into the persistent tier at startup, before
   159                      the fold (DESIGN.md section 8.6 P2d).
   160    --no-pins         con-ron's own, FOR TESTING: the empty pin list, the pin
   161                      loop's `[]` arm, under which a Nat.div/Nat.mod stream
   162                      declines.  Neither flag is needed for a normal run: the
   163                      pins are con-leche's `natOpPinSets`, embedded in the
   164                      verified core and decoded by it.  A run with either
   165                      flag is outside the proved theorems.
   166    --help            print this text on STDOUT and exit 0, in any argument
   167                      position; no input is read.  Its last line names the
   168                      global allocator THIS binary was built with (below), so a
   169                      measurement can be reproduced.
   170  
   171  build-time selection (cargo features, not command-line flags): the global
   172  allocator is `con-ron-dump`'s `#[global_allocator]`, chosen on this crate's
   173  dependency edge -- `cargo build --release` is mimalloc, `--no-default-features`
   174  is glibc `malloc`, and `--no-default-features --features jemalloc` is jemalloc.
   175  It is the same edge `crates/con-ron` has, so the two checkers are measured on
   176  the same allocator unless a build says otherwise.
   177  
   178  Any other option is a usage error: the run reports it, prints this text and
   179  exits 3 without reading its input.
   180  
   181  exit codes: 0 accepted, 1 rejected, 2 declined, 3 usage/malformed/internal.
   182  An out-of-memory condition is NEITHER: this program aborts the way Rust aborts
   183  on a failed allocation ('memory allocation of <n> bytes failed', SIGABRT,
   184  which a shell reports as 134).  A panic is exit 3.
   185  
   186  THE VERDICT LINE'S COUNT.  It counts the FILE's accepted declaration RECORDS:
   187  one per def/theorem/opaque/axiom/inductive/quot record the file declares.  The
   188  built-in prelude's own records are not counted, and neither are the records
   189  the in-process modeller generates; a stream record that declares a prelude
   190  declaration IS counted.  That count is a property of the INPUT; the number of
   191  environment CONSTANTS is not.
   192  
   193  THE BUILT-IN PRELUDE.  Every run installs, first and unconditionally, the
   194  checker's own little prelude -- the six pinned basis blocks (Eq, Nat, PUnit,
   195  Empty, False, Quot) and the toolchain's Bool and And blocks, embedded at build
   196  time -- so the pin-certified Nat operations find their ground whatever order
   197  the export chose.  It is parsed into the SAME store as the stream, which is
   198  what the persistent tier is for: the prelude's nodes and the stream's are
   199  hash-consed together.
   200  
   201  environment (con-leche's):
   202    CON_LECHE_INMODEL=0          turn the in-process modeller off; a mutual or
   203                                 nested block is then pushed bare and the FOLD
   204                                 declines it, having found no route
   205    CON_LECHE_INMODEL_CENSUS=1   report every mutual/nested block's outcome
   206                                 after the parse and stop (exit 2)
   207    CON_LECHE_PROJREC_TRACE      name each rewritten projection function
   208  These are the in-process modeller's debug switches.  None of them can make a
   209  run accept what the default rejects or declines: INMODEL=0 makes a mutual or
   210  nested block decline (exit 2), CENSUS=1 stops after the parse, before any
   211  check (exit 2), and PROJREC_TRACE only adds output.  The proved theorems
   212  (--verified) cover every setting of INMODEL and CENSUS.";

== proof/ConRon/Capstone.lean#L14-L144
    14  # `ConRon.Capstone` — THE COMPOSITION: Theorem 2 ∘ Theorem 1 ∘ con-leche
    15  
    16  DESIGN.md §8.2's last line: *"Capstones for the binary = Theorem 2 ∘
    17  Theorem 1 ∘ con-leche."*  This is the one module that imports both
    18  `ConRon.Bridge` (Theorem 1, (B) ⇒ (A)) and `ConRon.Refine2` (Theorem 2,
    19  (C) ⇒ (B)), and it states the binary's two headline theorems in the shape
    20  the original campaign used (`conron.model_exists` /
    21  `conron.no_False_declaration`, `proof/ConRon/RefineOld/Main.lean`):
    22  
    23  * `ConRon.Capstone.model_exists` — every environment the Aeneas model of the
    24    Rust pipeline accepts has a model in every set theory;
    25  * `ConRon.Capstone.no_False_declaration` — a file that declares a theorem of
    26    type `False` is never accepted by it.
    27  
    28  **They are the campaign's root theorems** (task #97-COMPOSE): the sorry
    29  frontier is measured as the dependency closure of these two, and it is
    30  EMPTY since `arena` `db1131f1` (task #97-MILESTONE): both depend on
    31  `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]` only (§5's census).  What they
    32  still assume is exactly their premises, listed below.
    33  
    34  ## The pipeline, stage by stage
    35  
    36  The binary (`crates/con-ron/src/bin/con-ron.rs`) is an unverified driver
    37  around six extracted core functions and the pin decoder, in this order, on
    38  one `AState` made from `EStore::empty()` and one `PersTier::empty()`:
    39  
    40      intern_reserved_pins → builtin_prelude_e → parse_source
    41        → prepare_prelude → (decode) → intern_all_pins → (the declaration fold)
    42  
    43  The headlines (§4) take one premise per call, from the binary's own start
    44  values `startState`/`emptyTier` (§3); §4's table maps each premise to its line
    45  of `check_main`.
    46  
    47  and the twin's `Arena.runPipeline` (`Arena/Main.lean`) is the same six
    48  stages with `installThenCheck` last.  **The sixth stage is the fold the
    49  binary's driver runs, pool and all** (task #97-P5-POOL):
    50  `driver::check_decls_driver` runs phase A with the heartbeat as its hook,
    51  freezes the tier, runs phase B on `pool::parallel_all`, and thaws the tier.
    52  The headlines take one premise per step (`h6` phase A, `h7` the freeze, `h8`
    53  phase B), which `poolAccepts_intro` assembles into
    54  `Refine2/Checker/Phased.lean`'s `PoolAccepts`.  Phase B's premise `h8` is
    55  the contract of the generic combinator `pool::parallel_all` with the driver's
    56  two verified closures, written out (task #98-H8): index lists `ws`, one per
    57  worker, covering every pending record, and for each a `foldlM` of
    58  `check_pending` over its indices from `worker_state`, accepting.  That
    59  contract is the pool's trusted claim (OVERVIEW §8.2): control flow of
    60  `pool.rs`, nothing about the checker.  `parallelAll_of_pool` reads it as
    61  `Phased.lean`'s `ParallelAll`, and `PoolAccepts.toParts` turns that into one
    62  accepting fold per worker over the records it checked.  The sequential walk
    63  `check_decls_phased` is one such pool (`poolAccepts_of_check_decls_phased`).
    64  The theorems hold for EVERY install hook, so they cover the plain run and
    65  `--progress` alike.  `pool_accepts_refines` relates the stage to the twin's
    66  `Arena.PooledAccepts`, and `Bridge/Checker/Phased.lean`'s
    67  `Arena.pooledAccepts_bridge` carries that to the pure fold.  So the
    68  statement takes the six Rust RUNS as premises (that the binary's
    69  `check_main` makes exactly these calls, in this order, is the one trusted
    70  line, exactly as it was for the original campaign), and the proof is:
    71  
    72  1. **Theorem 2, per stage** — `Refine2`'s six `…_refines` lemmas walk the
    73     Rust runs into six TWIN runs from the twin's own start state
    74     `AState.init EStore.empty`, related at every step (`AStateRel₀`/
    75     `AStateInv`: lockstep);
    76  2. **Theorem 1** — the twin runs feed `Arena.pooledAccepts_bridge`, whose
    77     pure fold accepts the denoted stream: con-leche's
    78     `checkDeclsPure_sound_of` gives the model, and
    79     `no_False_theorem_accepted_pure` refutes a `False` theorem in the stream
    80     (`stages_no_False`, `Arena.no_False_declaration_pipeline`'s route through
    81     the pure fold);
    82  3. **con-leche** — `checkDeclsPure_sound_of` turns the pure accept into a
    83     model.
    84  
    85  Every step is an existing theorem; what this file adds is glue: the Rust
    86  runs threaded through `Sim₀`/`SimStream`/`SimFold`, and the one twin-store
    87  fact the composition needs from Theorem 1 — `StoreWF` at the headline's
    88  `AStateRel` (`stages_storeWF`) — read off its stage lemmas.  Theorem 2 itself
    89  carries no fact about the twin's store (task #97-T2-AUDIT).
    90  
    91  ## The named hypotheses
    92  
    93  Since task #98-HEADLINE the headlines start from the binary's own start
    94  values (`startState` = `AState::empty()`, `emptyTier` = `PersTier::empty()`)
    95  instead of quantifying over a start state with `hpers`/`hest`/`hst0`
    96  equations, name the call the binary makes at each step (`prepare_d`, not
    97  `prepare_prelude`), and take the flags as parameters.  Beside
    98  `[ConLeche.SetTheory V]`, the file's shape `hfalse` and the one premise per
    99  call (`h1`…`h5`, `hpins`, `h6`…`h8`), what they assume is exactly:
   100  
   101  * `hmr : ModellerRefines inst m inProcessModeller` — the Rust modeller
   102    against the twin's (the modeller seam, by design): the unextracted
   103    `crates/con-ron/src/in_model/`, a port of con-leche's `InModel.generate`,
   104    answers what the twin's `inProcessModeller` (which CALLS con-leche's
   105    `generate`) answers;
   106  * `hreads : ReadsAs sinst src chunks.val` — the reads are the chunks
   107    (task #97-P5-Driver): the binary parses with the verified reader loop
   108    `parse_source` over the driver's file handle, and
   109    `Refine2/Frontend/Source.lean`'s `parse_source_eq` makes that
   110    `parse_chunks` over the chunks the handle hands out; that the handle hands
   111    out the file's bytes, in order, is the input seam, as `hmr` is the
   112    modeller's.
   113  
   114  Former hypotheses, now theorems or gone (DESIGN.md's task #97-COMPOSE and
   115  #98-HEADLINE sections tag each with its owning lane):
   116  
   117  * ~~`InitRel`~~ — the Rust start state is related to the twin's: a theorem
   118    since task #97-P5-Top (`Refine2/Checker/Init.lean`'s `init_rel`);
   119  * ~~`hk : CoreSpec .verified Arena.checkFuel`~~ — Theorem 1's Core tier
   120    spec: a theorem since task #97-P3-Core round 6
   121    (`Bridge/Checker/Hyp.lean`'s `CoreSpec.of_core`);
   122  * ~~`hind : IndSpec .verified`~~ — Theorem 1's inductive tier spec:
   123    `Bridge/Inductives/Decl.lean`'s `indSpec_of_bridge` since task #97-P3-Ind
   124    round 8 (the stage lemmas below still take it as a parameter);
   125  * ~~`hbytes`~~ — the prelude's bytes are con-leche's: not needed since task
   126    #98-HEADLINE.  con-leche's `preparePrelude` puts the prelude's records into
   127    the checked stream, so soundness holds whatever the prelude parses to
   128    (`Bridge/Frontend/Prepare.lean`'s `builtinPreludeE_run` is parametric in
   129    the bytes).  The gate `scripts/gen-prelude-lean.sh --check` stays, as the
   130    claim that con-ron ships con-leche's prelude;
   131  * ~~`hsc : ScanSpec`~~ — Theorem 2's scanner seam: a theorem since task
   132    #97-P5-Front (`Refine2/Frontend/Scan/Spec.lean`'s `scanSpec`);
   133  * ~~`hpers`, `hest`, `hst0`~~ — the start state and tier were universally
   134    quantified with three equations; since task #98-HEADLINE they are the
   135    constants `startState`/`emptyTier` (`startState_eq`, `emptyTier_eq`);
   136  * `hdec` is now `hpins`, the premise for the binary's pin step: the pin list
   137    is what the verified decoder read, at any text (as con-leche's theorems
   138    hold at every pin list); `model_exists_embedded` /
   139    `no_False_declaration_embedded` fix the text to the embedded `PINS_TEXT`;
   140  * ~~`in_model = true`, `census = false`~~ — the two environment flags
   141    (`CON_LECHE_INMODEL`, `CON_LECHE_INMODEL_CENSUS`; task #97-COMPOSE's
   142    mismatch 4): parameters since task #98-HEADLINE, so a run with either flag
   143    set is inside the theorems.
   144  -/

== proof/ConRon/Refine2/Frontend/Source.lean#L36-L40
    36  def ReadsAs {S : Type} (inst : frontend.export_c.ChunkSource S) :
    37      S → List (alloc.vec.Vec Std.U8) → Prop
    38    | src, [] => ∃ e src', inst.next_chunk src = ok (e, src') ∧ e.val = []
    39    | src, c :: cs => c.val ≠ [] ∧
    40        ∃ src', inst.next_chunk src = ok (c, src') ∧ ReadsAs inst src' cs

== proof/ConRon/Refine2/Frontend/Shape.lean#L662-L667
   662  structure ModellerRefines {G : Type} (inst : frontend.types.Modeller G) (m : G)
   663      (lmd : Arena.Frontend.Modeller) : Prop where
   664    generate : ∀ {pers rst lst rc lc b o},
   665      AStateRel₀ pers rst lst → AStateInv pers rst → CtxRel rc lc →
   666      inst.generate m pers rst.store rc b = ok o →
   667      SimGen pers rst lst o (lmd.generate lc (absBlockRec b))

   324      /// five entry-point memos, the `defeq` verdict table, the two
   325      /// level-verdict tables and the three lazy instantiated-constant tables.
   326      /// A record of its own beside `memos`, because the per-call clear and the

   331      /// `Sort 1`, interned ONCE into the persistent tier by the driver's
   332      /// `intern_all_pins` and read by handle ever after.  Empty until then,
   333      /// which is what makes a premature read a stop rather than a wrong
   334      /// answer (task #97c's hazard).

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/handle.rs#L4-L15
     4  //! One 32-bit word per handle:
     5  //!
     6  //! ```text
     7  //! bits 31…28   ctor tag   (4 bits, high)
     8  //! bit  27      tier       (0 = persistent, 1 = scratch)
     9  //! bits 26…0    index      into THAT CONSTRUCTOR'S array of THAT TIER
    10  //! ```
    11  //!
    12  //! so 134 217 728 nodes per constructor per tier, and — the point of putting
    13  //! the tier *above* the index rather than in the low bit (con-leche's lesson
    14  //! 6) — a persistent handle's bits never change when the scratch tier comes
    15  //! and goes.

   166  /// into the **binder datum store**: the same word layout as the other four (tag

   172  /// a `PropWhen` is `Arc`-carrying at `one`/`two`/`many`, so every `dup2` of a
   173  /// binder record is a reference count and every cons probe of the binder
   174  /// tables compares one (task #97-P6-10 §3 priced the pair at 2–3 % of
   175  /// `Init`).  With the datum interned the record is three `u32`s of POD, its
   176  /// hash is `pack2`-shaped like the other nine, and its `eq2` is three word
   177  /// comparisons.

   179      pub word: u32,
   180  }

  4155      /// whole sequence over the `ENodeView`, and each of its four steps
  4156      /// dispatched on the view's tag again and built the node record again:
  4157      /// the persistent probe built it (inside `ETables::find`), the scratch
  4158      /// probe built it a second time, `der_of_view` re-dispatched to compute
  4159      /// the derived word, and `ETables::push` re-dispatched and built it a
  4160      /// third time to append it.  A binder paid `binder_meta_dup` at each of
  4161      /// the three.  So the tag is read once here and the ten per-constructor
  4162      /// paths below each build their record ONCE and hand the same `&r` to the
  4163      /// two probes, to the capacity test and to the push — the same clauses in
  4164      /// the same order, with the dispatch and the two rebuilds gone.
  4165      ///
  4166      /// The twin's `intern` is one `def` over `ENodeView`; what is owed is the
  4167      /// ten-arm spelling and `internC v = intern (view of C)` per constructor,
  4168      /// each of them `rfl` after the `match`.
  4169      pub fn intern(&mut self, pers: &PersTier, v: ENodeView) -> Result<EIdx, CheckError> {
  4170          match v {
  4171              ENodeView::BVar(i) => self.intern_bvar(pers, i),
  4172              ENodeView::FVar(idx, ty) => self.intern_fvar(pers, idx, ty),
  4173              ENodeView::Sort(u) => self.intern_sort(pers, u),
  4174              ENodeView::Const(n, us) => self.intern_const(pers, n, us),
  4175              ENodeView::App(f, a) => self.intern_app(pers, f, a),
  4176              ENodeView::Lam(ty, body, m) => self.intern_lam(pers, ty, body, m),
  4177              ENodeView::ForallE(ty, body, m) => self.intern_forall_e(pers, ty, body, m),
  4178              ENodeView::LetE(ty, val, body) => self.intern_let_e(pers, ty, val, body),
  4179              ENodeView::Lit(l) => self.intern_lit(pers, l),
  4180              ENodeView::Proj(n, i, e) => self.intern_proj(pers, n, i, e),
  4181          }
  4182      }
  4183  

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/store.rs#L4433-L4479
  4433      pub fn intern_app(&mut self, pers: &PersTier, f: EIdx, a: EIdx) -> Result<EIdx, CheckError> {
  4434          let r: AppNode = AppNode { f, a };
  4435          let sk: bool = if self.scratch_on {
  4436              if r.f.is_persistent() {
  4437                  !r.a.is_persistent()
  4438              } else {
  4439                  true
  4440              }
  4441          } else {
  4442              false
  4443          };
  4444          let hit: Option<EIdx> = if sk {
  4445              None
  4446          } else if pers.frozen {
  4447              pers.e.apps.find(&r)
  4448          } else {
  4449              self.pers.apps.find(&r)
  4450          };
  4451          match hit {
  4452              Some(hp) => Ok(hp),
  4453              None => {
  4454                  if self.scratch_on {
  4455                      let at: (usize, Option<EIdx>) = self.scr.apps.find_slot(&r);
  4456                      match at.1 {
  4457                          Some(hs) => Ok(hs),
  4458                          None => {
  4459                              if self.scr.apps.full() {
  4460                                  Err(CheckError::Native(code_points(&M_E_CAP)))
  4461                              } else {
  4462                                  let d: u64 = self.der_of_app(pers, &r.f, &r.a);
  4463                                  let h: EIdx =
  4464                                      EIdx::pack(ETAG_APP, TIER_S, self.scr.apps.size() as u32);
  4465                                  self.scr.apps.push_at(at.0, r, d, h.dup2());
  4466                                  Ok(h)
  4467                              }
  4468                          }
  4469                      }
  4470                  } else if self.pers.apps.full() {
  4471                      Err(CheckError::Native(code_points(&M_E_CAP)))
  4472                  } else {
  4473                      let d: u64 = self.der_of_app(pers, &r.f, &r.a);
  4474                      let h: EIdx = EIdx::pack(ETAG_APP, TIER_P, self.pers.apps.size() as u32);
  4475                      self.pers.apps.push(r, d, h.dup2());
  4476                      Ok(h)
  4477                  }
  4478              }
  4479          }

 11695  /// con-leche: none — **the per-declaration bracket, closed** (DESIGN.md §8.3)
 11696  /// Lean twin: `proof/ConRon/Arena/Core.lean:3895-3903 dropScratch` — drop the

 11699  /// the tier `enter_scratch` handed out comes back (task #98-FREEZE), so the

 11707  /// Lean twin: `proof/ConRon/Arena/Core.lean:3905-3912 enterScratch` — turn the

     1  //! `arena::promote` — the scratch → persistent copy (DESIGN.md §8.3, task #97-P6-2).
     2  //!
     3  //! The Rust twin of `proof/ConRon/Arena/Promote.lean`, declaration for
     4  //! declaration, under DESIGN.md §8.6's lockstep ruling.
     5  //!
     6  //! DESIGN.md §8.3, "**Phase A runs in the scratch tier too, with promotion**":
     7  //!
     8  //! > The install phase (annotate the type and the value, infer, defeq) was
     9  //! > interning every intermediate into the persistent tier — on `Init` 5.06 M
    10  //! > permanent nodes on top of the parse's 6.14 M (+82 %) […].  The arena's
    11  //! > answer is con-leche #64's: phase A opens the scratch tier like phase B,
    12  //! > and the two handles it must keep (the annotated type, the annotated
    13  //! > value) are **promoted** — a memoised structural copy scratch →
    14  //! > persistent […] before the tier is dropped.  Persistent handles are
    15  //! > promoted to themselves.
    16  //!
    17  //! This module is that copy, at all four handle kinds and lifted to
    18  //! `arena::env`'s declaration layer, plus `promote_new` — the entry
    19  //! `arena::checker`'s two fold steps call, which promotes a step's NEWLY
    20  //! INSTALLED constants in place.
    21  //!
    22  //! ## What it is
    23  //!
    24  //! `view` the node, promote its children, `intern` the result into the
    25  //! PERSISTENT tier (`arena::store`'s `intern_persistent` family, whose section
    26  //! note carries the WF obligations).  Three properties make it cheap and make
    27  //! it right:
    28  //!
    29  //! * **a persistent handle promotes to itself**, by one tier-bit test
    30  //!   (`is_persistent`) and no store access at all.  Most of an annotated term
    31  //!   IS the parsed term — `annotate` rebuilds only the spine it changes — so
    32  //!   the walk stops at the first persistent node on every branch;
    33  //! * **the memo makes it `O(result)`** and not `O(unfolding)`: the subject is
    34  //!   a hash-consed DAG, and an unmemoised structural copy of a DAG is the
    35  //!   mistake task #97g's item 5 found three times over.  The memo is per
    36  //!   DECLARATION — a scratch handle means nothing once the tier is dropped —
    37  //!   and it is threaded as an argument-and-result pair, a moved
    38  //!   `ron::HashMap` returned, which is `frontend::proj_rec`'s spelling for its
    39  //!   `seen` set and `arena::expr_ops`' for the three memoized scope walks;
    40  //! * **`intern_persistent` probes the persistent cons table first**, so

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/checker.rs#L1408-L1430
  1408  /// con-leche: none — the phase boundary, which con-leche has no tier to make
  1409  /// Lean twin: none — the twin has no tier to move; its phase-B worker reads the
  1410  /// persistent tier where it is (`AState.worker`, `Arena/Phased.lean`).
  1411  /// **The persistent tier out of the store and into a value** (task
  1412  /// #97-P6-6b's driver function, moved here by task #97-P5-Driver): the four
  1413  /// persistent tables move into one `PersTier` handed back `frozen`, for the
  1414  /// phase-B workers to read.  Task #98-FREEZE: this is a pure MOVE — the
  1415  /// store's scratch tiers and flags are untouched (a worker's store is its own,
  1416  /// `worker_state`), there is no flag to test and so no decline (`M_REFREEZE`
  1417  /// is gone), and `thaw_tier` puts the tables back where they were.  The
  1418  /// driver's store is not read between the two.
  1419  pub fn freeze_tier(ar: &mut EStore) -> PersTier {
  1420      let n: NTables = core::mem::replace(&mut ar.lss.ls.ns.pers, NTables::empty());
  1421      let l: LTables = core::mem::replace(&mut ar.lss.ls.pers, LTables::empty());
  1422      let ls: LsTables = core::mem::replace(&mut ar.lss.pers, LsTables::empty());
  1423      let e: ETables = core::mem::replace(&mut ar.pers, ETables::empty());
  1424      PersTier {
  1425          frozen: true,
  1426          n,
  1427          l,
  1428          ls,
  1429          e,
  1430      }

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/core_state.rs#L525-L572
   525  /// con-leche: none — arena infrastructure (task #97-PERF-WALKMEMO)
   526  /// The slot count past which `take_walk_memo` hands back a FRESH table
   527  /// instead of a cleared one; see its note for how the value was chosen.
   528  pub const WALK_MEMO_KEEP: usize = 1 << 16;
   529  
   530  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Kernel/Level.lean:405-407 Expr.allLevelParamsDefinedFast
   531  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Kernel/DeclCheck.lean:197-199 Expr.constsResolveFFast
   532  /// Lean twin: the `∅` that `proof/ConRon/Arena/CheckerBase.lean`'s
   533  /// `allLevelParamsDefined` and `constsResolveFFast` start their walk from —
   534  /// **the parked walk memo, moved out of the state and emptied** (task
   535  /// #97-PERF-WALKMEMO).  The slot is left holding `HashMap::new()` (which
   536  /// allocates nothing) for the length of the walk, and the entry puts the
   537  /// grown table back afterwards; either way the table this returns is empty,
   538  /// so the walk starts where the twin's does.
   539  ///
   540  /// **nanoda's guard** (`nanoda_lib/src/expr.rs`, `inst`): a table past
   541  /// `WALK_MEMO_KEEP` slots is dropped rather than kept, so that one huge walk
   542  /// does not leave a huge table behind for every later call.  `reset_map`'s
   543  /// `clear_fit` already decays such a table, one eighth of its high-water mark
   544  /// a call, so the guard only decides which of the two is cheaper for an
   545  /// outlier: re-growing from nothing, or `clear_fit`'s re-make at the decayed
   546  /// size.  The threshold, measured on `Init` (`--verified --jobs=1`, one
   547  /// `perf stat -e instructions:u` run each, all accepting 57 977):
   548  ///
   549  /// | `WALK_MEMO_KEEP` | instructions:u |
   550  /// |---|---:|
   551  /// | fresh `HashMap::new()` per call (before) | 211 976 016 505 |
   552  /// | 2^10 slots (nanoda's 1024) | 208 379 555 799 |
   553  /// | 2^12 | 206 572 063 910 |
   554  /// | 2^14 | 205 851 105 938 |
   555  /// | **2^16** | **205 785 515 243** |
   556  /// | no guard (2^60) | 205 783 023 575 |
   557  ///
   558  /// A guard low enough to trip on ordinary calls gives the saving back — at
   559  /// nanoda's 1024 more than half of it — because those calls re-grow by
   560  /// doubling, which is exactly the cost this table exists to avoid.  2^16 is
   561  /// the smallest power tried that costs nothing measurable on `Init` (2.5 M
   562  /// instructions over no guard), so it only ever fires on an outlier.
   563  pub fn take_walk_memo<K, V>(slot: &mut HashMap<K, V>) -> HashMap<K, V> {
   564      let m: HashMap<K, V> = core::mem::replace(slot, HashMap::new());
   565      if m.capacity() > WALK_MEMO_KEEP {
   566          HashMap::new()
   567      } else {
   568          let mut m2: HashMap<K, V> = m;
   569          reset_map(&mut m2);
   570          m2
   571      }
   572  }

== crates/con-ron-core/src/ron/hashmap2.rs#L1-L40
     1  //! con-leche: none — arena infrastructure; a second `Std.HashMap` replacement, proved
     2  //!
     3  //! `ron::HashMap2<K, V>` — proved in `proof/ConRon/Refine/HashMap2.lean`
     4  //! (task #97-HM2; designed in task #97-P6-4b).  The same abstract object as
     5  //! `ron::hashmap`'s `HashMap` — a partial map from `K` to `V`, with
     6  //! `Hashable`/`Eq2`/`Dup` as its dictionaries and the same eleven operations
     7  //! — over an **open-addressed, epoch-stamped, flat slot vector** instead of
     8  //! the Aeneas tutorial's chained buckets.  `ron::hashmap` is untouched and
     9  //! keeps its proofs (`proof/ConRon/Refine/HashMap.lean`); this module's are
    10  //! in `proof/ConRon/Refine/HashMap2.lean` (task #97-HM2).
    11  //!
    12  //! **Why it exists.**  Task #97-P6-1 left `clear_slots + allocate_slots +
    13  //! move_elements*` at 21.8 % of `Init`, "all halving recursions over chained
    14  //! buckets".  Task #97-P6-4b counted what those recursions actually do on
    15  //! `Init`, and the counts name the representation rather than the code:
    16  //!
    17  //! | on `Init`, `ron::HashMap` | count |
    18  //! |---|---:|
    19  //! | `get` calls | 1 228 953 968 |
    20  //! | — resolved in 0 or 1 chain step | 98.8 % |
    21  //! | `insert` calls | 627 320 951 |
    22  //! | **`clear` calls** | **36 053 620** |
    23  //! | **— buckets walked by them** | **2 940 488 064** |
    24  //! | — entries those buckets held | 586 917 896 |
    25  //! | buckets pushed by `allocate_slots` | 948 184 512 |
    26  //! | entries moved by `move_elements*` | 349 323 629 |
    27  //!
    28  //! So the chains are *already* short — the table is a good hash table — and
    29  //! essentially all of the 21.8 % is the per-bucket cost of **emptying and
    30  //! re-growing** the slot vector: 2.94 G bucket writes to clear 0.59 G entries
    31  //! (five buckets walked per entry cleared; the average cleared table is 82
    32  //! buckets holding 16 entries) and 0.95 G `Vec::push`es to allocate them back.
    33  //! Nothing a better chain walk can do touches that.
    34  //!
    35  //! **The representation.**
    36  //!
    37  //! * `slots : Vec<Slot<K, V>>`, `Slot` = `Vacant | Live(u32, K, V)`.  No
    38  //!   `Box`, no chain, no allocation per entry — an entry *is* a slot.
    39  //! * A `Live` slot is **live only if its stamp is the table's `epoch`**;
    40  //!   a `Live` slot with a stale stamp is free space, indistinguishable from

   358  fn check_main(a: &Args, file: &str) -> u8 {
   359      let t0 = Instant::now();
   360      let mode_tag = if a.verified {

   372      // ConRon.Capstone: `startState`

   376      // is owned (not frozen) outside a declaration bracket — so what they are

   461              }
   462          },
   463          Ok((Ok(r), _)) => r,

   513      let gen_records = parsed.gen_records;
   514      // From here on the store is the checker's state: the memo tables and the

   517      // **PREPARE** (`frontend::prepare`): what the fold runs over is

   523      // ConRon.Capstone: h4

   525          Ok(p) => p,
   526          Err(e) => return frontend_exit(&e, mode_tag),
   527      };
   528      // the ground hoist's receipt
   529      if !prepared.hoisted.is_empty() {
   530          let names: Vec<String> = prepared
   531              .hoisted
   532              .iter()

   539              names.join(", ")
   540          );
   541      }
   542      // ConRon.Capstone: hpins (`decode_embedded`; `--pins`/`--no-pins` are
   543      // outside the theorems)
   544      let pins = match con_ron::driver::pins_for_run(&a.pins, a.no_pins) {

   546          Err(e) => {

   548              return 3;
   549          }
   550      };
   551      // The heartbeat's first line: the parse and the preparation are done.
   552      let mut hb = Heartbeat::new(a.progress, t0);
   553      hb.parse_done(

   585      // a run with one and `install_then_check` is no longer a second path.

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/pins.rs#L1-L60
     1  //! `arena::pins` — the reserved names, interned ONCE (task #97-P6-4a).
     2  //!
     3  //! con-leche compares its reserved names — `natName`, `natZeroName`,
     4  //! `natSuccName`, the sixteen `Nat`-operation names, the `Bool` trio, the
     5  //! `String`/`List`/`Char` family, the standard and the trusted axiom names —
     6  //! as `Name` VALUES, which Lean builds once per nullary `def` and caches.
     7  //! The arena compares them as HANDLES, so `arena::core::pin` turned each one
     8  //! into `intern_name` of a freshly built `Name`: a `code_points` allocation
     9  //! and an `Arc<NameNode>` per path segment, then one cons-table probe per
    10  //! segment, every time.  Task #97-P6-1's counter measured what that costs on
    11  //! `Init`: **140 083 646 `NStore::intern` calls, of which 88 854 033 are
    12  //! probes of a `str` node built purely to be compared and dropped** — tens of
    13  //! millions of rebuilds of about forty constants, in `natLitSupported`'s
    14  //! three probes per literal, in `natOpNames`, in `strLitToConstructor`.
    15  //!
    16  //! This module is DESIGN.md's answer, flagged at task #97c ("the `Pins`
    17  //! record that is NOT here") and deferred there for want of a number: one
    18  //! record, filled once at the driver by `intern_reserved_pins`, and every
    19  //! `pin` of a constant name becomes a field read.
    20  //!
    21  //! **Not `arena::checker`'s `intern_all_pins`.**  That one walks the `--pins`
    22  //! RECEIPT file (the trusted pin list) into the persistent tier; this one
    23  //! interns the checker's own reserved constants.  The two run at the same
    24  //! point of the pipeline and mean different things, which is why they have
    25  //! different names.
    26  //!
    27  //! ## The table is a `Vec`, and that is what kills task #97c's hazard
    28  //!
    29  //! Task #97c declined the record because of an initialisation-order hazard:
    30  //! "a pin read before it is filled compares against the zero word and
    31  //! silently says *not `Nat`*".  A record of handle FIELDS has that hazard,
    32  //! because every 32-bit word is a syntactically valid handle.  A `Vec<NIdx>`
    33  //! does not: before `intern_reserved_pins` runs the table is EMPTY, so `pin_at`
    34  //! takes its bounds branch and raises `CheckError::Internal` — a loud stop,
    35  //! never a quiet wrong answer.  The cost is one `len` compare per read,
    36  //! against an interning walk it replaces.
    37  //!
    38  //! ## What is pinned
    39  //!
    40  //! The forty-nine names below and `basis_names::reserved_basis_names()`'s
    41  //! nineteen, plus the three interned values every `pin` site around them
    42  //! needs: the empty universe-argument list, the level `0` and the expression
    43  //! `Sort 1` (`arena::core`'s `empty_levels`, `zero_level` and `sort_one`,
    44  //! which now read this record instead of interning).
    45  //!
    46  //! All of them go into the PERSISTENT tier, because `intern_reserved_pins` runs
    47  //! before the parse, while the scratch tier is closed.  That matters twice:
    48  //! a pinned handle must survive every `drop_scratch` (it is read across all
    49  //! of them), and task #97-P6-1's `pers_find_maybe` rests on "a persistent
    50  //! node's children are persistent", which the bottom-up intern of a closed
    51  //! scratch tier gives for free.
    52  //!
    53  //! **Denotation unchanged.**  A pin is `intern_name` of the same `Name`, so
    54  //! the handle this record holds is the handle `pin` computed before —
    55  //! `denoteN` is injective and `intern` is idempotent, so pre-interning a name
    56  //! the export also carries hands the export's parse the very same handle.
    57  //! What changes is only WHEN the intern happens, and how many times.
    58  //!
    59  //! Lean twin: `proof/ConRon/Arena/Monad.lean:119-136 AState` (DESIGN.md §8.6's
    60  //! twin ledger, task #97-P6-4a) — `AState` gains a `pins : Pins` field and

== crates/con-ron-core/src/frontend/prepare.rs#L1-L50
     1  //! `proof/ConRon/Arena/Frontend/Prepare.lean` — **what happens between the
     2  //! file and the fold** (task #97 P4e part 1).
     3  //!
     4  //! `prepare_prelude` is total — no record of the stream is dropped, rewritten
     5  //! or retagged — and it does two things:
     6  //!
     7  //! 1. **the prelude's declarations first**, the stream's OWN copy of each
     8  //!    where the stream has one and a synthesised one only where it has none,
     9  //!    so a stream that declares the toolchain's `Bool` is checked on its own
    10  //!    `Bool` record;
    11  //! 2. **the ground hoist**: a pinned `Nat` operation's stream-certified
    12  //!    structural ground is moved ahead of it when the stream declares it
    13  //!    later.
    14  //!
    15  //! Moving a record earlier can only reject, never accept, which is why the
    16  //! spec con-leche proves is as simple as it is:
    17  //!
    18  //! ```text
    19  //! ∃ extra, (∀ d ∈ extra, d ∈ prelude) ∧
    20  //!   (preparePrelude ds).toList.Perm (ds.toList ++ extra)
    21  //! ```
    22  //!
    23  //! **Step 2 is `frontend::nat_op_ground`'s**, a module of its own exactly as
    24  //! con-leche's is (task #97-P4d; task #97-P4e part 1 shipped an identity
    25  //! placeholder here, because the pass needs the kernel's
    26  //! `natOpNames`/`natDivModNames`, which arrived with the pins).  It is why
    27  //! `prepare_d` takes the whole `AState` where everything else in this module
    28  //! needs only the store.
    29  //!
    30  //! **Where the store comes from.**  Only `prelude_key`, whose `.anonymous`
    31  //! fall-through has to be INTERNED, and the two functions that call it;
    32  //! [`pick_idx`] and [`declares`] are pure, exactly as con-leche's are, because
    33  //! `env::i_declaration_names` is (`arena/env.rs`'s `table_name` note).
    34  //! Nothing in this module reads or writes a term.
    35  //!
    36  //! **The deviation of the port into the verified core** (task #84), kept
    37  //! verbatim from `con_ron_core::frontend::prepare`: con-leche's `pick` ERASES
    38  //! the picked record from the array (`Array.eraseIdxIfInBounds`) and `frontOf`
    39  //! moves it to the front.  The Aeneas subset has no operation that takes an
    40  //! element out of a `Vec` — no `remove`, no `pop`, no `into_iter` — so the
    41  //! port splits the two halves that con-leche fuses: [`pick_idx`] is the cited
    42  //! `ds.findIdx (declares n)` with the erasure recorded in a `picked` mask
    43  //! instead of performed, [`front_of`] runs that over the prelude, and
    44  //! [`prepared_stream`] materialises the whole prepared list in ONE pass.  The
    45  //! list that comes out is the same list; the cost is one record copy per
    46  //! record, where the copied fields are handles and `Vec` spines and not terms.
    47  //! con-leche's `pickSpec`/`frontSpec` are not ported (they are `cons`-list
    48  //! specifications with no caller on the run path); `pick_spec` lives in this
    49  //! module's tests, where it still checks `pick_idx` against the specification
    50  //! on every `cargo test`.

  1572  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Kernel/NatOpPins.lean:62-65 _
  1573  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Kernel/BasisA.lean:50-57 BasisKind.declsA
  1574  /// Lean twin: `proof/ConRon/Arena/Checker.lean:472-508 internAllPins` — **the
  1575  /// one-time tree walk of DESIGN.md §8.6 P2d**: every datum the checker compares
  1576  /// a stream record against, interned into the tier that is live at the call —
  1577  /// which, at the driver's call, is the persistent one.
  1578  ///
  1579  /// The six basis blocks in both forms (the RAW ones `basis_pin_hit` and
  1580  /// `quot_pin_hit` compare against, the ANNOTATED ones `check_basis_decl`
  1581  /// installs), the standard and compiler-trust axiom pins, the reserved names
  1582  /// the guards compare by handle, and the `Nat`-operation pin variants, whose
  1583  /// interned form is the checker's pin-list parameter (con-leche's task #304).
  1584  pub fn intern_all_pins(
  1585      pers: &PersTier,
  1586      st: &mut AState,
  1587      pins: &Vec<NatOpPinSet>,
  1588  ) -> Result<Vec<INatOpPinSet>, CheckError> {
  1589      match intern_all_basis(pers, st, 0) {
  1590          Err(e) => Err(e),
  1591          Ok(()) => match intern_all_axiom_pins(pers, st) {
  1592              Err(e) => Err(e),
  1593              Ok(()) => match intern_all_names(st) {
  1594                  Err(e) => Err(e),
  1595                  Ok(()) => intern_pin_sets(pers, st, pins, 0, Vec::new()),
  1596              },
  1597          },
  1598      }
  1599  }

  1325  /// **The decoder.**  `con-ron-pins/1` text in, con-leche's pin variants out,
  1326  /// in file order — which is the order `checker::check_div_mod_pin_loop` tries
  1327  /// them in, and therefore the order the list has to be in.
  1328  pub fn decode(t: &[u8]) -> CheckM<Vec<NatOpPinSet>> {
  1329      let hdr = pins_header();
  1330      if !starts_with_from(t, &hdr, 0) {
  1331          Err(bad_text())
  1332      } else {
  1333          run_records(t, hdr.len(), tables_new())
  1334      }

== crates/con-ron/src/driver.rs#L939-L984
   939  // `IO.FS.Handle.read` has no model, and a theorem about the file is a
   940  // theorem about its bytes.
   941  // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   942  
   943  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Frontend/ExportC.lean:903-931 parseExportHandleD
   944  /// **The file handle as the parse's `ChunkSource`**: each `next_chunk` is one
   945  /// `read_up_to` of `chunk` bytes, strictly forward, handed over whole; the
   946  /// first empty read is the end of the input.  A failed read ends the input
   947  /// the same way and is KEPT here, and `parse_export_handle_d` reports it in
   948  /// place of whatever the parse of the truncated input said — so a read error
   949  /// is exit 3, never a verdict, as before the loop moved.
   950  pub struct HandleSource<'a, R: Read> {
   951      /// The open reader.
   952      pub h: &'a mut R,
   953      /// The buffer size, `export_c::CHUNK_SIZE` in the binary.
   954      pub chunk: usize,
   955      /// The nonempty buffers handed out so far, for the heartbeat.
   956      pub chunks: u64,
   957      /// The first read failure, if any.
   958      pub err: Option<std::io::Error>,
   959  }
   960  
   961  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Frontend/ExportC.lean:903-931 parseExportHandleD
   962  impl<'a, R: Read> ChunkSource for HandleSource<'a, R> {
   963      /// con-leche: ConLeche/Frontend/ExportC.lean:903-931 parseExportHandleD
   964      /// One read of up to `chunk` bytes; empty at the end or on a failure.
   965      fn next_chunk(&mut self) -> Vec<u8> {
   966          if self.err.is_some() {
   967              return Vec::new();
   968          }
   969          let mut buf: Vec<u8> = vec![0u8; self.chunk];
   970          match read_up_to(self.h, &mut buf) {
   971              Ok(n) => {
   972                  buf.truncate(n);
   973                  if n > 0 {
   974                      self.chunks += 1;
   975                  }
   976                  buf
   977              }
   978              Err(e) => {
   979                  self.err = Some(e);
   980                  Vec::new()
   981              }
   982          }
   983      }
   984  }

   246  /// in, the model records it generates in stream order or the reason it is
   247  /// declined.  Handles in, handles out — nothing in (B) may build an `Expr`

   251  /// **Why a trait and not a function pointer** (`in_model_rec`'s reason,
   252  /// unchanged): a trait method on a type parameter extracts as a *typeclass
   253  /// field* — an opaque function of the quantified `Self` — so the extracted
   254  /// parse is quantified over an arbitrary modeller and a later refinement
   255  /// carries one hypothesis about its output rather than a port of four

   257  /// `dyn` object or a function pointer is outside the subset (DESIGN.md §3.4).

   259  /// The store is in hand because the twin's method is in `AM`: a generated
   260  /// record's terms are handles, and building one means interning it.

   268          ctx: &ModelCtx,
   269          b: &BlockRec,
   270      ) -> Result<Vec<IDeclaration>, Vec<u32>>;
   271  }

    10  //!
    11  //! ```text
    12  //! BlockRec over handles  --denote-->  con-ron-core's BlockRec (Expr trees)
    13  //!                                       |  crate::in_model::generate
    14  //!                                       v
    15  //! Vec<IDeclaration>      <--intern--  Vec<Declaration>
    16  //! ```
    17  //!
    18  //! **This is the twin's own instantiation, one representation down.**  The
    19  //! Lean reads the block back, calls *con-leche's* generator and interns what
    20  //! comes out; the Rust reads the block back, calls *con-ron's port of that
    21  //! generator* and interns what comes out.  So the two binaries of the
    22  //! differential sweep run the SAME unverified modeller: `con-ron` calls it on
    23  //! the trees its parser builds, `con-ron` calls it on the trees this
    24  //! module reads back out of the store.  A block modelled differently by the
    25  //! two would be a difference the sweep could not attribute, and there is now
    26  //! no way for one to arise.
    27  //!
    28  //! **Nothing here is verified and nothing here needs to be** (DESIGN.md §8.2,
    29  //! and con-leche's own module note): a wrong generated record is rejected or
    30  //! declined by the fold, never accepted, so this layer decides *coverage* and

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/checker.rs#L1-L40
     1  //! `arena::checker` — the declaration fold, over handles.
     2  //!
     3  //! The Rust twin of `proof/ConRon/Arena/Checker.lean`, which is con-leche's
     4  //! `Kernel/Checker.lean`'s `checkDecl`/`checkDeclsPure` and
     5  //! `Cached/Installed.lean`'s two-phase `checkDecls`.
     6  //!
     7  //! ## Two folds, and which is which
     8  //!
     9  //! * **`check_decls_pure`** is the THEOREM's shape —
    10  //!   `ConLeche/Model/Fold.lean`'s `checkDeclsPure_sound_of` consumes it, and
    11  //!   DESIGN.md §8.2's Theorem 1 folds `checkDecl` over the stream.  One step
    12  //!   per record, install and check together.
    13  //! * **`install_then_check`** is what the BINARY runs: phase A installs every
    14  //!   record, annotating its header and its value but not inferring; phase B
    15  //!   checks each recorded declaration against the PREFIX VIEW it was installed
    16  //!   at.  con-leche proves the two are the same accept
    17  //!   (`fullyChecked_checkDecls`); the arena's two call the same `checkDecl`
    18  //!   pieces, which is what keeps them the same computation.
    19  //!
    20  //! ## Every step is bracketed
    21  //!
    22  //! DESIGN.md §8.3: "Persistent = parse + installed environment; scratch = one
    23  //! declaration's check."  Both phases and both folds run each record inside
    24  //! `enter_scratch` … `drop_scratch`.  Phase B's `check_pending` brackets
    25  //! `check_value_group`, and every node it appends goes with the tier.  Phase
    26  //! A's `annot_step` brackets the install too (the fallback `annot_step_other`
    27  //! included), because annotation infers and inference interns: `promote`
    28  //! copies exactly what leaves the step — the installed constants and the
    29  //! pending record — to the persistent tier before the drop (see `annot_step`).
    30  //! `check_decls_pure`'s step, `check_decl_step`, is bracketed the same way.
    31  //!
    32  //! ## The pins are interned at startup
    33  //!
    34  //! `intern_all_pins` is DESIGN.md §8.6 P2d's one-time tree walk, and it is what
    35  //! makes every later `pin`/`intern_ci` of the same datum return the PERSISTENT
    36  //! handle whatever tier is live (§8.3: `intern` probes the persistent table
    37  //! first).  Without it a reserved name first interned inside a scratch tier
    38  //! would compare unequal to the stream's own persistent copy of it, which is
    39  //! the one way hash-consing can go wrong across the tier boundary.
    40  

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/checker.rs#L920-L960
   920  pub fn annot_step(
   921      _pers: &PersTier,
   922      st: &mut AState,
   923      mode: &CheckMode,
   924      pins: &Vec<INatOpPinSet>,
   925      i: u64,
   926      fe: IFEnv,
   927      pend: Vec<PendingCheck>,
   928      pd: &IDeclaration,
   929  ) -> Result<(IFEnv, Vec<PendingCheck>), CheckError> {
   930      let vis: u64 = fe.visible_below;
   931      flush_caches(st);
   932      let mut tier: PersTier = enter_scratch(st);
   933      match annot_step_go(&tier, st, mode, pins, fe, pd) {
   934          Err(e) => {
   935              drop_scratch(st, tier);
   936              Err(e)
   937          }
   938          Ok((fe2, vg_opt)) => {
   939              let k: u64 = fe2.visible_below - vis;
   940              match vg_opt {
   941                  None => match promote_new(&mut tier, st, PMemo::empty(), CORE_WALK_FUEL, k, fe2) {
   942                      Err(e) => {
   943                          drop_scratch(st, tier);
   944                          Err(e)
   945                      }
   946                      Ok((_, fe3)) => {
   947                          drop_scratch(st, tier);
   948                          Ok((fe3, pend))
   949                      }
   950                  },
   951                  Some(vg) => annot_step_promote(tier, st, i, vis, k, fe2, pend, vg),
   952              }
   953          }
   954      }
   955  }
   956  
   957  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Cached/Installed.lean:144-183 annotStepC
   958  /// Lean twin: `proof/ConRon/Arena/Checker.lean:329-383 annotStep` — the
   959  /// bracket's `some vg` arm: the seam promoted first and the environment at the
   960  /// SAME memo, then the tier dropped and the record pushed.

== crates/con-ron/src/driver.rs#L523-L619
   523  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Cached/Installed.lean:438-455 checkDecls
   524  /// con-leche: Main.lean:318-421 checkDeclsIO
   525  /// **The driver**: `checker::check_decls_phased` with the boundary visible —
   526  /// a straight line of calls, with the observer's lines between them and the
   527  /// pool in the place of phase B's sequential walk (tasks #97-P5-Driver,
   528  /// #98-POOL).  Each step is one premise of the capstone:
   529  ///
   530  /// | step | here | the capstone's premise |
   531  /// |---|---|---|
   532  /// | phase A | `checker::annot_fold_hooked(…, fold_start(), ds, 0, obs)` | the same call accepts |
   533  /// | boundary | `checker::freeze_tier(&mut st.store)` | the same call's value |
   534  /// | phase B | `pool::parallel_all(m, workers, ‖ worker_state(pins), ‖w, k‖ check_pending(&tier, w, mode, &fe, &pend[k]), …)` | `h8`: index lists `ws` covering `0..pend.len`, each `w` a `foldlM` of `check_pending tier st mode fe pend[k]` over `k ∈ w` from `worker_state pins`, accepting (internally `ParallelAll`) |
   535  /// | after | `checker::thaw_tier(&mut st.store, tier)` | restores the store (`freeze_tier_ok`) |
   536  ///
   537  /// `init` and `step` are calls into the verified crate; `parallel_all` is the
   538  /// one trusted piece, and its contract (`pool.rs`'s note) is exactly
   539  /// `ParallelAll`: on `Ok`, every record was checked by some worker,
   540  /// each worker folding `check_pending` over the records it claimed on ONE
   541  /// `worker_state`.  Everything else here is the observer, which only ever
   542  /// holds `&` the state (the hook of phase A by the trait's own signature, the
   543  /// other lines through `&st.store` and the worker's `&AState`), so it cannot
   544  /// change an outcome.
   545  ///
   546  /// **The boundary is where the tier is FROZEN** (task #97-P6-6b).  Phase A
   547  /// owns its persistent tier and appends to it; at the boundary
   548  /// `checker::freeze_tier` moves the four stores' persistent tables out into
   549  /// one `PersTier`, handed back `frozen`: every read through it goes to those
   550  /// tables, and a worker's own store is frozen (`checker::worker_state`), so
   551  /// every append there is a scratch append (task #98-FREEZE).  The
   552  /// installed index goes to the workers by reference, since `check_pending`
   553  /// takes the visibility bound as a scalar — so `n` workers share one
   554  /// environment and one term DAG and own nothing but a scratch tier, their
   555  /// caches and a copy of the pin handles (`checker::worker_state`).
   556  pub fn check_decls_driver<O: PhaseObserver + InstallHook + Send>(
   557      pers: &PersTier,
   558      st: &mut AState,
   559      mode: &CheckMode,
   560      pins: &Vec<INatOpPinSet>,
   561      ds: &Vec<IDeclaration>,
   562      jobs: u64,
   563      obs: &mut O,
   564  ) -> Result<IFEnv, (CheckError, u64)> {
   565      let total = ds.len();
   566      // PHASE A (ConRon.Capstone: h6): the verified fold, the heartbeat as hook.
   567      let p = match checker::annot_fold_hooked(pers, st, mode, pins, checker::fold_start(), ds, 0, &*obs) {
   568          Err(e) => {
   569              obs.install_failed(e.1, total);
   570              return Err(e);
   571          }
   572          Ok(p) => p,
   573      };
   574      let (_n_installed, fe, pend): (u64, IFEnv, Vec<PendingCheck>) = p;
   575      let m = pend.len();
   576      obs.install_done(pers, &st.store, total, m);
   577      let workers = workers_for(jobs, m);
   578      obs.phase_b_workers(workers);
   579      // THE PHASE BOUNDARY: the persistent tier leaves the state and becomes a
   580      // value every worker reads (the doc comment above).  `st` keeps its
   581      // (empty) store, its tables moved out, so the observer can still read a
   582      // label back through the tier.  (ConRon.Capstone: h7)
   583      let tier: PersTier = checker::freeze_tier(&mut st.store);
   584      // PHASE B: `check_pending` at every record, on `workers` threads, each
   585      // folding it over the records it claims on ONE `worker_state` — the
   586      // verdict and the record a rejection names are the one-worker walk's at
   587      // every `--jobs` (the least failing index).  (ConRon.Capstone: h8)
   588      let heartbeat = obs.wants_check_lines();
   589      let lock = Mutex::new(obs);
   590      let done = AtomicUsize::new(0);
   591      let r = parallel_all(
   592          m,
   593          workers,
   594          || checker::worker_state(&st.pins),
   595          |w: &mut AState, k| checker::check_pending(&tier, w, mode, &fe, &pend[k]),
   596          |w: &AState, k| check_line(heartbeat, &done, &lock, &tier, w, m, &pend[k]),
   597      );
   598      let obs: &mut O = match lock.into_inner() {
   599          Ok(o) => o,
   600          Err(e) => e.into_inner(),
   601      };
   602      // AND THE TIER GOES BACK.  Everything after the fold — the verdict line's
   603      // declaration label, the failing record's name, the receipts — reads a
   604      // handle back out of `st`, and a state left frozen over a tier that has
   605      // gone out of scope answers `None` to every one of them (the first
   606      // version of this printed `at theorem ?` where the tip printed `at
   607      // theorem addOk`).  `thaw_tier` is `freeze_tier` inverted.
   608      checker::thaw_tier(&mut st.store, tier);
   609      match phase_b_verdict(&pend, r) {
   610          Err((e, pos)) => {
   611              obs.check_failed(pos);
   612              Err((e, pos))
   613          }
   614          Ok(()) => {
   615              obs.check_done(m);
   616              Ok(fe)
   617          }
   618      }
   619  }

    30  //! ## What a worker is, in phase B
    31  //!
    32  //! §8.3 has said since P1 what phase B is: "the persistent tier is immutable
    33  //! in phase B, each worker owns a scratch tier — **no atomics anywhere**",
    34  //! and task #97-P6-6 verified it in the code (`check_pending` is the bracket;
    35  //! the persistent interns' only caller is phase A's `arena::promote`, which
    36  //! writes a `&mut PersTier` a worker never holds).  So the driver's `init`

    41  //! the installed `&IFEnv` (by reference: `check_pending` takes the record's

  1463  /// Lean twin: `proof/ConRon/Arena/Phased.lean:37-44 AState.worker` — the twin's

  1465  /// **A phase-B worker's start state** (task #97-P6-6b's `pool::worker_state`,

  1474      st

   227  /// con-leche: Main.lean:289-316 checkPool
   228  /// **`step` at every index of `0..n`, on a pool of `workers` threads** — the
   229  /// module note's trusted claim is this function's contract:
   230  ///
   231  /// > If it returns `Ok(())`, every index in `0..n` was claimed by exactly one
   232  /// > worker, each worker built its state with `init()` once and folded `step`
   233  /// > over its claimed indices in claim order (increasing), and every step
   234  /// > returned `Ok(())`.
   235  ///
   236  /// On a failure it returns the LEAST failing index with its error
   237  /// (`ParallelError::Step`), whatever the timing.  `after(&st, k)` runs on the
   238  /// worker's thread after each step it made, with the worker's state by `&`
   239  /// (the driver's heartbeat); it cannot change an outcome.
   240  ///
   241  /// The workers are `std::thread::scope`d, with `STACK_BYTES` of stack each.
   242  /// `workers` is the count the caller has already clamped
   243  /// (`driver::workers_for`: `max(1, min(jobs, n))`); if the OS refuses to
   244  /// spawn one, the pool runs on those it has, and on the calling thread if it
   245  /// has none — the contract holds at every worker count, so the answer does
   246  /// not depend on it.
   247  pub fn parallel_all<S, E: Send>(
   248      n: usize,
   249      workers: usize,
   250      init: impl Fn() -> S + Sync,
   251      step: impl Fn(&mut S, usize) -> Result<(), E> + Sync,
   252      after: impl Fn(&S, usize) + Sync,
   253  ) -> Result<(), ParallelError<E>> {

    87  pub enum CheckError {
    88      NotImplemented(Vec<u32>),
    89      Invalid(Vec<u32>),
    90      Internal(Vec<u32>),

   157  /// con-leche: Main.lean:48-51 ConLeche.CheckError.exitCode
   158  /// The cited three codes, plus the port's own fourth constructor
   159  /// (`core_types::CheckError::Native`, DESIGN.md §3's ruling of 2026-09-13):
   160  /// a failure with no con-leche counterpart — a machine-word limit, a width
   161  /// check — is a **decline**, exit 2, the same code as "not implemented",

   164  pub fn exit_code(e: &CheckError) -> u8 {

   166          CheckError::NotImplemented(_) => 2,
   167          CheckError::Invalid(_) => 1,
   168          CheckError::Internal(_) => 3,
   169          CheckError::Native(_) => 2,
   170      }

== proof/ConRon/Arena/Denote.lean#L181-L206
   181  /-- con-leche: ConLeche/Kernel/Expr.lean:344-354 Expr — the fuel-indexed
   182  readback of an expression handle. -/
   183  def denoteEAux (st : EStore) : Nat → EIdx → Option Expr
   184    | 0, _ => none
   185    | f + 1, i =>
   186      (st.view i).bind fun v =>
   187        match v with
   188        | .bvar k => some (.bvar k)
   189        | .fvar k ty => (denoteEAux st f ty).map (Expr.fvar k)
   190        | .sort u => (denoteL st.ls u).map Expr.sort
   191        | .const n us => opt2 Expr.const (denoteN st.ns n) (denoteLs st.lss us)
   192        | .app g a => opt2 Expr.app (denoteEAux st f g) (denoteEAux st f a)
   193        | .lam ty b m =>
   194          opt2 (fun x y => Expr.lam x y m) (denoteEAux st f ty) (denoteEAux st f b)
   195        | .forallE ty b m =>
   196          opt2 (fun x y => Expr.forallE x y m) (denoteEAux st f ty) (denoteEAux st f b)
   197        | .letE ty w b =>
   198          opt3 Expr.letE (denoteEAux st f ty) (denoteEAux st f w) (denoteEAux st f b)
   199        | .lit l => some (.lit l)
   200        | .proj n k e =>
   201          opt2 (fun nm x => Expr.proj nm k x) (denoteN st.ns n) (denoteEAux st f e)
   202  
   203  /-- con-leche: ConLeche/Kernel/Expr.lean:344-354 Expr — the readback of an
   204  expression handle, at the store's own node count as fuel. -/
   205  def denoteE (st : EStore) (i : EIdx) : Option Expr :=
   206    denoteEAux st (st.nodeCount + 1) i

== proof/ConRon/Arena/WF.lean#L1-L40
     1  /-
     2  # Store well-formedness and the store layer's theorems (DESIGN.md §8.3, P2a)
     3  
     4  `StoreWF` is the arena's own invariant — con-leche's `TWF`
     5  (`Setlec/Kernel/ArenaWF.lean:900`, 28 clauses) redrawn for the
     6  per-constructor, high-tag representation.  It lives here, beside the
     7  implementation, importing nothing from `ConRon.Refine`: con-leche's lesson 27,
     8  "implementation may import a *self-contained* data-structure verification".
     9  
    10  Each store's invariant is `∃ rank, …WFAt st rank`.  The rank is existential
    11  because nothing at runtime stores it (DESIGN §8.3: "zero runtime cost, and no
    12  global array order is needed with per-constructor arrays"); what it buys is
    13  
    14  * **acyclicity**, hence a terminating `denote`;
    15  * **a fuel bound**: a persistent node's rank is below the persistent node
    16    count and a scratch node's below the total, so `nodeCount + 1` — the fuel
    17    `denoteE` uses — is always enough, and `dropScratch` shrinks both sides of
    18    the persistent clause together.
    19  
    20  The clauses, in the order a reader meets them:
    21  
    22  | clause | what it says |
    23  |---|---|
    24  | `childOK` | every child is in range, ranked below its parent, and persistent if the parent is |
    25  | `rankP` / `rankS` | ranks are below the tier's node count (the fuel bound) |
    26  | `consP` / `consS` | each tier's cons table is exactly the inverse of that tier's `get` |
    27  | `fresh` | a scratch cons entry never duplicates a persistent one (DESIGN §8.3's cross-tier canonicity; con-leche's `t_cons_fresh`) |
    28  | `derExact` | the derived column is `derOfView` of the node — *locally*; the global `derived st i = e.data` is a theorem (`derived_exact`) |
    29  | `sized` | the derived array is as long as the node array |
    30  | `cap` | no constructor array exceeds 2^27 entries, so a handle's 27-bit index is injective on it |
    31  | `bmKey` | every binder key a cons table holds names a datum the store can decode |
    32  | `scrOff` | the scratch tier is empty while the scratch flag is off |
    33  | `sync` | the nesting's scratch flags move together (task #97a) |
    34  
    35  `childOK`'s third conjunct — *persistent parents have persistent children* —
    36  is what makes `dropScratch` sound: without it a persistent node could point
    37  into a tier that is about to vanish.  It needs no hypothesis at `intern`,
    38  because `scrOff` makes a scratch handle undecodable while the flag is off, so
    39  a valid child of a node appended to the persistent tier is persistent already.
    40  -/

== proof/ConRon/Bridge/Specs.lean#L1-L60
     1  /-
     2  # `ConRon.Bridge.Specs` — one `@[spec]` theorem per `Monad.lean` primitive
     3  
     4  The thing task #97s's spike exists to fix: **one spec theorem per (B)
     5  primitive, in one shape**, so that `mvcgen` can walk a twin's body without any
     6  store reasoning appearing in the proof text.  The shape is the spike's
     7  seven-rule template (DESIGN §8.6, `P2s SPIKE`, and task #97s's own section):
     8  
     9  ```lean
    10  @[spec] theorem f_spec (s₀ : AState) (args…) (pre…) :
    11      ⦃fun s => ⌜s = s₀⌝⦄ f args ⦃⇓? r s' => ⌜Post s₀ r s'⌝⦄
    12  ```
    13  
    14  1. **the precondition is `s = s₀` and nothing else** — every real
    15     precondition is an ordinary hypothesis of the theorem, so `mspec` turns it
    16     into a side goal instead of an entailment to discharge in the logic;
    17  2. **`⇓?` (partial correctness), never `⇓`** — a (B) function may fail and
    18     Theorem 1 claims nothing then (con-leche's `SimAt`,
    19     `Verify/SimI.lean:244`);
    20  3. **the postcondition names `s₀`**, the only way to state
    21     `Ext s₀.store s'.store` in a triple;
    22  4. **"the subject denotes" is an `isSome`, never a named `Expr`**;
    23  5. **the answer is a named relation** (`Bridge/Rel.lean`'s `RelE` family),
    24     never a bare `∀ e, … → …`;
    25  6. **a memo insert's spec states that the INVARIANT is preserved**, not that
    26     the table grew — the single highest-value change of the spike;
    27  7. **one named failure primitive** (`fail`), because a bare `throw` in
    28     `StateT σ (Except ε)` leaves `mvcgen` with universe metavariables.
    29  
    30  ## The frame conditions
    31  
    32  `AState` has four fields and the `Memos` record has thirteen tables, so a
    33  naive frame condition would be sixteen equations per spec.  Task #97b put the
    34  per-call tables in ONE record and task #97c the per-declaration ones in
    35  another for exactly this reason: every spec below frames the state in at most
    36  four equations, and a memo write frames the other twelve tables with one
    37  (`s'.memos = { s₀.memos with xC := … }`).
    38  
    39  `Bridge/StateOK.lean`'s `CheckOK.mono` is what those equations buy: the whole
    40  checker invariant crosses an `ExprOps` call on `Ext` plus
    41  `s'.caches = s₀.caches` plus `s'.pins = s₀.pins`.
    42  
    43  ## What is NOT here, and why
    44  
    45  * **`internPersistentE` / `…N` / `…L` / `…Ls`.**  `Arena/Store.lean`'s own
    46    note (the section "Interning into the PERSISTENT tier") states the
    47    obligation for the BRACKET and not for the operation: `internPersistent`
    48    breaks `fresh` transiently, and it is `promote … dropScratch` as a whole
    49    that takes `StoreWF` to `StoreWF`.  Its four specs therefore belong to the
    50    `Promote` tier, whose statement is that bracket, not to this file.
    51  * **the eleven `internRebuilt*` faces of `ExprOps.lean`** are here, at the
    52    end: they are `internE` plus task #97-P6-5's upward cutoff, and every
    53    rebuilding walk goes through them.
    54  
    55  ## The closer
    56  
    57  `bridge_vcs` at the end of this file is task #97s round 2's recipe: ONE
    58  curated `grind` list, a `bridge_peel` in front of it, and a second stage that
    59  puts the `RelE` transports back for the handful of verification conditions
    60  that genuinely have to move an answer along the extension chain.  The arm

   184  def PSpec {α : Type} (P : EStore → Prop) (c : AM α) (R : EStore → α → Prop) :
   185      Prop :=
   186    ∀ (s₀ s' : AState) (r : α), StateOK s₀ → P s₀.store → c s₀ = .ok (r, s') →
   187      PStep s₀ s' ∧ R s'.store r
   188  
   189  /-- con-leche: none — the empty precondition, for a twin whose arguments are
   190  all `Nat`s. -/
   191  abbrev PT : EStore → Prop := fun _ => True
   192  
   193  /-- con-leche: none — **the PURE grade AT A PIN READ** (task #97-P3-Ind round
   194  3's finding; see `Bridge/Inductives/StructParts.lean`'s `structProjGuards_spec`).
   195  
   196  `PSpec`'s precondition is a predicate on the STORE, so it cannot see the pin
   197  table — and `Arena/Pins.lean`'s `pinsReady` tests only that the name array has
   198  `pinCount` entries, not that any of the three nullary slots denotes what it
   199  claims.  A twin that reads `zeroLevel`, `sortOne` or `emptyLevels` therefore
   200  has no `PSpec`: at a state whose `pins.zeroLevel` denotes `.param foo` the
   201  run ACCEPTS and answers something else.  `PinsOK` is the missing licence, and
   202  this is the only shape that carries it while keeping `PStep`: the twin is
   203  still pure — it interns and reads, it calls no knot — so dropping to `CSpec`
   204  (the other statement that has `PinsOK`, through `CheckOK`) would give away the
   205  `BMExt` and cache-frame conjuncts for nothing. -/

   213  theorem PSpec.toPSpecP {α : Type} {P : EStore → Prop} {c : AM α}
   214      {R : EStore → α → Prop} (h : PSpec P c R) : PSpecP P c R :=
   215    fun s₀ s' r hok _ hp hrun => h s₀ s' r hok hp hrun

== proof/ConRon/Bridge/Inductives/StructParts.lean#L168-L213
   168  /-! ## The families and the spines -/
   169  
   170  /-- con-leche: ConLeche/Kernel/Inductives/StructParts.lean:134-137 structPsAt
   171  The parameter variables as seen from under `o` extra binders.
   172  
   173  **CLOSED** (task #97-P3-Ind round 2): a `Nat` recursion over
   174  `internBVarE_run` with the cursor `k` generalised.  The pure side is a
   175  `List.range` map, so the step is `List.range_succ_eq_map` and one `omega` on
   176  the index arithmetic (`k + (j + 1) = k + 1 + j`). -/
   177  theorem structPsAt_go_run (o nP : Nat) : ∀ (n k : Nat) {s s' : AState}
   178      {r : List EIdx}, StateOK s → Arena.structPsAt.go o nP n k s = .ok (r, s') →
   179      PStep s s' ∧ Frontend.denoteEList s'.store r
   180        = some ((List.range n).map fun j => Expr.bvar (o + nP - 1 - (k + j))) := by
   181    intro n
   182    induction n with
   183    | zero =>
   184      intro k s s' r hok hrun
   185      simp only [Arena.structPsAt.go] at hrun
   186      obtain ⟨rfl, rfl⟩ := pureOk hrun
   187      exact ⟨PStep.refl hok, rfl⟩
   188    | succ n ih =>
   189      intro k s s' r hok hrun
   190      simp only [Arena.structPsAt.go] at hrun
   191      obtain ⟨b, s₁, h1, h2⟩ := bindOk hrun
   192      obtain ⟨rest, s₂, h3, h4⟩ := bindOk h2
   193      obtain ⟨hstep1, hb⟩ := internBVarE_run hok h1
   194      obtain ⟨hstep2, hrest⟩ := ih (k + 1) hstep1.ok h3
   195      obtain ⟨rfl, rfl⟩ := pureOk h4
   196      refine ⟨hstep1.trans hstep2, ?_⟩
   197      have hkey : ((List.range (n + 1)).map fun j => Expr.bvar (o + nP - 1 - (k + j)))
   198          = Expr.bvar (o + nP - 1 - k) ::
   199            ((List.range n).map fun j => Expr.bvar (o + nP - 1 - (k + 1 + j))) := by
   200        rw [List.range_succ_eq_map, List.map_cons, List.map_map]
   201        congr 1
   202        refine List.map_congr_left (fun j _ => ?_)
   203        simp only [Function.comp_apply]
   204        congr 1
   205        omega
   206      rw [hkey]
   207      simp only [Frontend.denoteEList, denote_ext hb hstep2.ext, hrest]
   208  
   209  theorem structPsAt_spec (o nP : Nat) :
   210      PSpec PT (Arena.structPsAt o nP) (REL (ConLeche.structPsAt o nP)) := by
   211    intro s₀ s' r hok _ hrun
   212    obtain ⟨hstep, hd⟩ := structPsAt_go_run o nP nP 0 hok hrun
   213    refine ⟨hstep, ?_⟩
